mandate.target: once a day: every memory dir is under its cap (10,240 B / 50 entries) with duplicates merged and resolved entries dropped, and $FLEET_LOG_DIR/INTENT.md (<=40 lines) says what the human decided, corrected and asked for in the last 14 days -- read by dumbledore, marie and gru at the start of their passes
checklist: run members/librarian/memory_tend.py --execute and read its per-dir report: size/entries vs cap, dead lines removed, orphans, resolved candidates, similar pairs
merge near-duplicates, drop resolved entries whose lesson lives in code or a charter, index or delete orphans, bring MEMORY.md under cap -- Edit/Write inside the memory dir only, never raise the cap

run members/librarian/intent_digest.py (captures + asks + Reif: comments) and write $FLEET_LOG_DIR/INTENT.md: standing decisions, corrections/reversals, open asks; short quotes with dates, never a secret
0 captures in the listing is a finding: the capture cron on the human's machine stopped -- name it for a human
a lesson recurring across several members is a charter bug: name it for dumbledore, never edit a charter
credential classes librarian-scrub keeps finding name a leaking member; a shape it cannot see is a gap for a human, never a hand-written regex
mandate.escalation: a memory dir you cannot bring under cap without losing a live lesson, or a pattern gap in the scrubber: say so in the report as the one thing a human must decide. Never touch /repo, /fleet-kit or any charter.

schedule.note: UTC; entrypoint.sh line `15 5 * * *`. Once a day on purpose (fleet-kit#784): the hourly scrub is librarian-scrub, a shell member.
